comments.author: @SecAk-nyc
comments.text: İstanbul is an unusual city, there’s no another one like that in the world. Istanbul conveys many different cultures; the Western, Eastern, Arabic, and everyone respects each other’s culture and heritage. I used to live in New York, so the rent and food were very expensive there too. Istanbul is a real democratic place to live. You have to be careful every big city. Generally, some people can earn less money,  but you rarely find people who are living on the streets like Western countries. The video is narratively well done. The cars are double price in Turkey than Europe and America. Thanks.

comments.text: The contrast between neighborhoods like Kadıköy and Fatih is spot on. You can travel through five different centuries and mindsets within a single 20-minute bus ride.

comments.author: @Reallifeinsights.26
comments.text: Here, no matter how high inflation climbs, the local shop owner still opens up for the day with a spirit of resilience and perseverance.

comments.author: @HienCam-v9u
comments.text: The rent vs. minimum wage breakdown hits WAY too hard. Istanbul is absolute heaven to visit with foreign currency, but my heart goes out to the locals hustling through 30%+ inflation every single day.

comments.author: @GlobalLifeInsights
comments.text: Skip the overpriced rooftop tourist traps! Find a quiet neighborhood Meyhane in Besiktas or Kadikoy, order cold meze with a bottle of Rakı, and let the live music play for 4 hours. THAT is the real Istanbul night.

comments.author: @EpicWorldDiscoveries-m2g
comments.text: Istanbul has spent centuries balancing Islamic tradition and Western influence, but which side shapes daily life more today? Is the city losing its identity—or is this cultural contradiction its true identity?

comments.author: @RealLifeFilesDoc
comments.text: A city that calls itself Muslim yet drinks, dresses, and debates like the West. A place where you can see a woman in a bikini and another in a traditional hijab walking down the street on the exact same afternoon. Istanbul isn't the East, nor is it the West; it's a world that refuses all stereotypes and labels. This blend is absolutely mesmerizing! What cultural aspect of this city do you love the most? 🇹🇷🌍
